DESCRIPTION: A 25U is the Army's premier radio and tactical communication expert. They install, maintain, and troubleshoot VHF/UHF radios, satellite terminals, and their associated encrypted networks across all types of vehicles and command posts.

NAME: Paralegal Specialist
DESCRIPTION: This soldier assists Army Judge Advocates in providing legal services to the command and individual soldiers. They prepare legal documents, assist with military justice proceedings (such as Article 15s and courts-martial), and provide administrative support for legal assistance.

NAME: Military Intelligence Officer
DESCRIPTION: A Military Intelligence Officer leads soldiers in gathering, analyzing, and disseminating intelligence about enemy forces, terrain, and weather. They advise commanders on enemy capabilities and intentions to shape tactical planning.

NAME: Intelligence Analyst
DESCRIPTION: An Intelligence Analyst processes and evaluates incoming information from multiple sources to create a coherent picture of the battlefield. They build enemy templates, brief commanders on threat capabilities, and assist in targeting hostile forces.

NAME: Human Resources Specialist
DESCRIPTION: This soldier manages the administrative and personnel needs of the unit, including promotions, awards, leaves, and evaluations. They ensure that soldiers' records are accurate and that personnel readiness is maintained for deployment.

NAME: Human Resources Officer
DESCRIPTION: A Human Resources Officer manages personnel systems, manning levels, and postal operations for a command. They advise commanders on soldier morale, administrative policies, and the deployment readiness of the force.

NAME: Command and Unit Chaplain
DESCRIPTION: A Chaplain is a commissioned officer who provides religious support, spiritual counseling, and moral guidance to soldiers and their families. They advise the commander on the religious and ethical climate of the unit while safeguarding the free exercise of religion.

NAME: Religious Affairs Specialist
DESCRIPTION: This soldier partners with the unit Chaplain to provide religious support and crisis intervention to soldiers. They manage chapel operations, provide physical security for the unarmed Chaplain, and assist in counseling coordination.

NAME: Emergency Physician
DESCRIPTION: An Emergency Physician is an Army medical officer who specializes in the rapid assessment, resuscitation, and stabilization of acute illnesses and combat trauma. They serve as the primary life-savers in forward surgical teams and combat support hospitals.

NAME: Field Surgeon
DESCRIPTION: A Field Surgeon is a medical officer responsible for providing comprehensive medical care and trauma stabilization in a deployed environment. They often serve as a battalion surgeon, advising the commander on the health and medical readiness of the unit.

NAME: General Dentist
DESCRIPTION: An Army General Dentist provides comprehensive dental care to soldiers, focusing on preventative maintenance and the treatment of oral diseases. In deployed settings, they treat maxillofacial trauma, perform emergency tooth extractions, and ensure the unit is dentally ready to deploy.

NAME: Physical Therapist
DESCRIPTION: An Army Physical Therapist is a commissioned officer who evaluates and treats soldiers suffering from musculoskeletal injuries. They play a crucial role in rehabilitation, injury prevention, and returning wounded or injured troops to combat readiness.

NAME: Physician Assistant
DESCRIPTION: A Physician Assistant is a medical provider who examines, diagnoses, and treats soldiers under the supervision of a physician. They often serve as the primary medical provider at the battalion aid station level, managing both routine sick call and combat trauma.

NAME: Medical-Surgical Nurse
DESCRIPTION: A Medical-Surgical Nurse is a registered nurse and commissioned officer who provides specialized nursing care to patients with complex medical and surgical conditions. They work in field hospitals and medical centers to monitor patients, administer medications, and assist in recovery.

NAME: Behavioral Science Officer
DESCRIPTION: A Behavioral Science Officer is a mental health professional who provides psychological evaluations, counseling, and psychiatric care to soldiers. They assist commanders in managing combat stress and ensuring the mental resilience of the unit.

NAME: Biomedical Equipment Specialist
DESCRIPTION: This soldier is a highly trained technician responsible for servicing, calibrating, and repairing life-saving medical equipment such as ventilators and X-ray machines. They ensure that all hospital technology functions flawlessly in austere environments.

NAME: Dental Specialist
DESCRIPTION: A Dental Specialist assists Army dentists during examinations and surgical procedures, acting similarly to a civilian dental hygienist or assistant. They prepare dental instruments, take X-rays, and manage clinic administration.

NAME: Physical Therapy Specialist
DESCRIPTION: This soldier works under the supervision of a physical therapist to help soldiers recover from physical injuries. They guide patients through rehabilitative exercises, administer modalities like cold therapy, and fit orthopedic devices.

NAME: Patient Administration Specialist
DESCRIPTION: This soldier manages medical records, patient tracking, and hospital admissions and dispositions. In a combat zone, they are vital for tracking casualties as they move from the point of injury through the medical evacuation chain.

NAME: Medical Logistics Specialist
DESCRIPTION: A Medical Logistics Specialist procures, stores, and distributes medical supplies, blood products, and hospital equipment. They ensure that medics and doctors have an uninterrupted supply of the specialized items needed to save lives.

NAME: Medical Laboratory Specialist
DESCRIPTION: This soldier performs clinical laboratory tests on blood, urine, and tissue to help doctors diagnose diseases and treat injuries. They operate complex lab equipment and manage the military blood banking system in field hospitals.

NAME: Radiology Specialist
DESCRIPTION: A Radiology Specialist operates X-ray and ultrasound equipment to produce medical images of a patient's body. These images are critical for diagnosing bone fractures, locating shrapnel, and assessing internal trauma in a combat setting.

NAME: Pharmacy Specialist
DESCRIPTION: This soldier prepares and dispenses prescribed medications under the supervision of a pharmacist. They maintain pharmacy inventory, verify dosages, and ensure that deployed units have access to critical drugs and IV fluids.

NAME: Preventive Medicine Specialist
DESCRIPTION: A Preventive Medicine Specialist conducts environmental health surveys to protect soldiers from diseases and non-battle injuries. They test water quality, inspect food service facilities, and monitor base camps for insect vectors and toxic hazards.

NAME: Combat Medic Specialist
DESCRIPTION: The Army's primary front-line medical provider. They are trained in Tactical Combat Casualty Care to administer emergency medical treatment at the point of injury, stabilize wounded soldiers, and coordinate their medical evacuation.

NAME: Behavioral Health Specialist
DESCRIPTION: This soldier assists behavioral health officers in providing mental health counseling and crisis intervention to troops. They conduct intake interviews, teach stress management classes, and monitor patients experiencing combat stress.

NAME: Health Services Administration Officer
DESCRIPTION: A Medical Service Corps officer responsible for the administrative and logistical leadership of medical units. They command medical companies, manage hospital operations, and plan the tactical employment of medical assets.

NAME: Health Services Plans, Operations, Intelligence, Security, and Training Officer
DESCRIPTION: An officer who specializes in the deliberate planning and operational execution of medical missions. They coordinate medical evacuation coverage, hospital placements, and health service support for large-scale combat operations.

NAME: Health Services Materiel Officer
DESCRIPTION: This officer is a medical logistics expert who manages the complex supply chains required to equip and sustain military hospitals. They oversee the procurement and distribution of pharmaceuticals, medical gases, and hospital equipment.

NAME: Environmental Science and Engineering Officer
DESCRIPTION: An officer who assesses and mitigates environmental and occupational health risks to deployed forces. They analyze water quality, industrial hazards, and disease vectors to prevent non-battle casualties and protect force health.

NAME: Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN) Specialist
DESCRIPTION: This soldier is trained to detect, identify, and decontaminate CBRN hazards on the battlefield. They operate sensitive detection equipment, conduct specialized reconnaissance, and train other soldiers on surviving in a toxic environment.

NAME: Motor Transport Operator
DESCRIPTION: A soldier responsible for operating wheeled tactical vehicles to transport personnel, ammunition, and supplies. They are the backbone of Army logistics, driving everything from utility trucks to heavy equipment transporters in convoy operations.

NAME: Transportation Management Coordinator
DESCRIPTION: This soldier schedules and coordinates the movement of personnel and cargo by air, rail, highway, and water. They act as logistical traffic controllers, ensuring that supplies and units flow efficiently across the global supply chain.

NAME: Ammunition Warrant Officer
DESCRIPTION: An Ammunition Warrant Officer is the unit's technical expert on the storage, handling, and maintenance of all conventional ammunition and explosives. They oversee ammunition supply points and ensure compliance with strict explosive safety regulations.

NAME: Ammunition Stock Control and Accounting Specialist
DESCRIPTION: This soldier manages the complex digital and manual inventory systems for military explosives and ammunition. They track the receipt, storage, and issuance of munitions to ensure units have the correct firepower for their missions.

NAME: Ammunition Specialist
DESCRIPTION: An Ammunition Specialist physically handles, stores, and issues all types of conventional ammunition, from small arms bullets to artillery shells. They are trained in explosive safety, load configurations, and the destruction of unexploded ordnance.

NAME: Logistics Officer
DESCRIPTION: A Logistics Officer plans and directs the multifaceted supply, maintenance, and transportation operations required to sustain an Army force. They command logistics units and integrate all classes of supply into the commander's tactical plan.

NAME: Armament Systems Maintenance Warrant Officer
DESCRIPTION: A technical expert who oversees the repair and maintenance of complex weapon systems, including tank turrets and artillery pieces. They advise commanders on the readiness of the unit's armament and supervise lower-enlisted mechanics.

NAME: Allied Trades Warrant Officer
DESCRIPTION: A Warrant Officer who serves as the subject matter expert on metalworking, machining, and welding operations. They supervise allied trades specialists and design custom metal fabrication solutions to repair damaged combat equipment.

NAME: Automotive Maintenance Warrant Officer
DESCRIPTION: An Automotive Maintenance Warrant Officer directs and manages the maintenance and repair of the unit's wheeled and tracked vehicle fleet. They troubleshoot complex mechanical failures and oversee the motor pool's workflow and quality control.

NAME: Engineer Equipment Maintenance Warrant Officer
DESCRIPTION: A technical expert who manages the maintenance program for heavy construction and combat engineering equipment. They supervise the repair of bulldozers, excavators, and bridging systems essential for mobility operations.

NAME: M1 Abrams Tank System Maintainer
DESCRIPTION: This soldier is a specialized mechanic trained to troubleshoot and repair the mechanical and electrical systems of the M1 Abrams main battle tank. They maintain the tank's turbine engine, transmission, and heavy suspension.

NAME: Wheeled Vehicle Mechanic
DESCRIPTION: The Army's primary mechanic for light, medium, and heavy tactical trucks. They perform preventive maintenance, replace engines and transmissions, and recover disabled vehicles to keep the logistics fleet rolling.

NAME: Utilities Equipment Repairer
DESCRIPTION: This mechanic specializes in maintaining and repairing field environmental control units, air conditioners, and heaters. Their work is critical for protecting sensitive electronics and preventing heat or cold injuries among personnel.

NAME: Tactical Power Generation Specialist
DESCRIPTION: A mechanic trained specifically to repair and maintain the Army's fleet of diesel generators. They ensure that tactical operations centers, hospitals, and communication nodes have a continuous and reliable supply of electricity.

NAME: Allied Trades Specialist
DESCRIPTION: This soldier is a skilled welder and machinist capable of fabricating custom metal parts from scratch. They repair damaged vehicle frames, apply emergency armor, and manufacture tools when supply chains cannot deliver replacement parts.

NAME: Small Arms/Towed Artillery Repairer
DESCRIPTION: An armorer and mechanic who inspects, maintains, and repairs everything from rifles and machine guns to towed howitzers. They ensure that all unit weaponry fires accurately and functions reliably in combat.

NAME: Tracked Vehicle Repairer
DESCRIPTION: A mechanic specializing in the repair of armored tracked vehicles, such as the M113 personnel carrier and M88 recovery vehicle. They work on heavy diesel engines, complex drive trains, and the heavy metal tracks that provide vehicle mobility.

NAME: Quartermaster and Chemical Equipment Repairer
DESCRIPTION: This soldier maintains specialized logistical equipment, including water purification systems, field kitchens, and chemical decontamination apparatuses. They ensure that the essential life-support systems of a deployed unit remain operational.

NAME: Bradley Fighting Vehicle System Maintainer
DESCRIPTION: A highly trained mechanic dedicated to the upkeep of the M2/M3 Bradley Fighting Vehicle. They diagnose and repair the vehicle's diesel engine, transmission, suspension, and integrated fire control systems.

NAME: Stryker Systems Maintainer
DESCRIPTION: This mechanic is responsible for maintaining the Stryker family of eight-wheeled armored vehicles. They perform complex diagnostics and repairs on the vehicle's drivetrain, pneumatic suspension, and electronic systems.

NAME: Maintenance Supervisor
DESCRIPTION: A senior non-commissioned officer who directs the daily operations of a maintenance platoon or motor pool. They manage mechanics across multiple specialties, coordinate repair parts, and advise the commander on equipment readiness.

NAME: Senior Maintenance Supervisor
DESCRIPTION: The highest-level enlisted maintenance leader in a battalion or brigade, responsible for overseeing all maintenance operations. They manage the careers of junior mechanics, enforce quality control, and ensure the entire vehicle and equipment fleet is combat-ready.

NAME: Property Accounting Technician
DESCRIPTION: A Warrant Officer who serves as the unit's absolute authority on property accountability and supply regulations. They manage the complex digital ledgers and hand receipts that track millions of dollars' worth of military equipment.

NAME: Automated Logistical Specialist
DESCRIPTION: This soldier operates the Army's digital supply systems to order, track, and issue repair parts and equipment. They manage warehouse inventories and ensure that mechanics receive the correct components to fix broken vehicles.

NAME: Petroleum Supply Specialist
DESCRIPTION: A soldier responsible for receiving, storing, testing, and issuing bulk petroleum products. They operate heavy fuel tankers and pumping stations to refuel vehicles and aircraft, ensuring the force has the energy required to maneuver.

NAME: Culinary Specialist
DESCRIPTION: This soldier prepares and serves meals in garrison dining facilities and mobile field kitchens. They are trained in food safety, nutrition, and operating containerized kitchens to sustain the morale and health of deployed troops.

NAME: Fatality Management Specialist
DESCRIPTION: A specialized soldier responsible for the respectful recovery, processing, and evacuation of deceased military personnel. They operate mortuary affairs collection points to ensure fallen soldiers are handled with dignity and returned home.

NAME: Water Treatment Specialist
DESCRIPTION: This soldier operates highly technical reverse osmosis water purification units (ROWPU) to turn raw, contaminated water into safe drinking water. They test for chemical and biological purity to sustain life in austere environments.

NAME: Unit Supply Specialist
DESCRIPTION: The core supply sergeant of a company or detachment, responsible for ordering, receiving, and issuing individual gear, weapons, and daily supplies. They maintain the commander's property books and ensure soldiers are properly equipped.

NAME: Senior Noncommissioned Logistician
DESCRIPTION: A senior enlisted leader who oversees broad logistical operations for a battalion or brigade. They coordinate supply, transportation, and services to ensure the entire formation is sustained during extended combat operations.

NAME: Electronic Systems Maintenance Warrant Officer
DESCRIPTION: A technical expert who directs the maintenance and repair of advanced radar, missile, and communication systems. They train junior electronics repairers and manage the test equipment required to troubleshoot complex circuitry.

NAME: Land Combat Electronic Missile System Repairer
DESCRIPTION: This soldier diagnoses and repairs the electronic and optical guidance systems of ground-based anti-tank weapons, like the TOW and Javelin missiles. They ensure that these critical tank-killing systems are perfectly calibrated.

NAME: Radio Equipment Repairer
DESCRIPTION: An electronics technician specializing in the deep-level repair of tactical radios, satellite terminals, and their cryptographic modules. They use oscilloscopes and signal generators to find and replace faulty microchips and circuit boards.

NAME: Computer/Detection Systems Repairer
DESCRIPTION: This soldier maintains and repairs specialized tactical computers, GPS receivers, and mine detection equipment. They possess advanced skills in soldering and component-level electronic troubleshooting.

NAME: Radar Repairer
DESCRIPTION: A highly trained technician who diagnoses and repairs ground-based radar systems used for air defense and artillery tracking. They work on massive antennas, high-voltage power supplies, and delicate signal processors.

NAME: Electronic Maintenance Supervisor
DESCRIPTION: A senior non-commissioned officer who manages the shop operations for a team of electronic repairers. They prioritize work orders, manage test equipment calibration, and ensure the rapid return of critical communication and weapon systems.

NAME: Automatic Test Systems Operator/Maintainer
DESCRIPTION: This soldier operates and repairs complex, computerized diagnostic benches used to test a wide variety of electronic components. They use these automated systems to isolate faults in line replaceable units (LRUs) faster than manual testing allows.

NAME: Senior Electronic Maintenance Supervisor
DESCRIPTION: The highest-ranking enlisted expert in electronic maintenance within a large unit. They advise the commander on the readiness of all radar, missile, and communication systems and orchestrate the training of the electronic maintenance force.

NAME: Armament Repair Shop Set (ARSS)
DESCRIPTION: This is a mobile, shelter-mounted maintenance workshop equipped with specialized fixtures, hand tools, and testing apparatus. It is used by armament repair technicians to inspect, service, and repair small arms, crew-served weapons, and artillery components in field environments. The system provides expeditionary maintenance capability without requiring permanent shop facilities.

NAME: Tactical Environmental Control Unit (TECU)
DESCRIPTION: This is a military-grade, skid-mounted heating and air conditioning unit engineered to operate in austere environments. It is used to provide conditioned air to tactical command posts, mobile shelters, and sensitive electronic equipment enclosures. It operates on military standard tactical electrical power and withstands extreme temperature variations.

NAME: Tactical Environmental Control Unit (TECU)
DESCRIPTION: This is a ruggedized mobile air conditioning and climate control system designed for tactical field shelters and command vehicles. It provides reliable cooling, dehumidification, and ventilation to maintain habitable operational conditions and prevent overheating of mission-critical electronics. The unit is designed for rapid integration with standard military shelter ducts and power grids.

NAME: Tactical Shipping and Storage Container
DESCRIPTION: This is a heavy-duty, reusable protective transport container engineered with custom foam cushioning and pressure relief valves. It is used to store and transport sensitive tactical equipment, optics, or missile components securely across land, sea, and air logistics chains. Its watertight and shock-resistant construction prevents damage during harsh expeditionary movements.

NAME: Compact Air Conditioner, 18,000 BTU
DESCRIPTION: This is a compact, high-capacity tactical environmental control unit capable of providing 18,000 BTU/hr of cooling capacity. It is primarily used to cool tactical shelters, mobile command posts, and communication vans operating in high-temperature climates. The unit features a hardened frame and operates reliably on standard military diesel generator power.

NAME: ME-563/U Clamp-On Digital Multimeter
DESCRIPTION: This is a handheld electronic test instrument featuring an integrated inductive clamp mechanism. It allows technicians to measure alternating and direct current, voltage, and resistance without physically breaking or interrupting electrical circuits. It is a vital troubleshooting tool used by automotive and electronic repairers across tactical fleets.

NAME: MK-2868/G Accessory Kit, Electronic Equipment
DESCRIPTION: This is a field accessory kit containing specialized connection leads, test probes, mounting hardware, and peripheral adapters. It supports tactical electronics and communication shelters by enabling rapid interconnection and interface with various external systems. All items are organized in a weather-resistant carrying case for mobile field operations.

NAME: OE-254/GRC Antenna Group
DESCRIPTION: This is an omnidirectional, biconical tactical antenna group designed for VHF-FM combat net radios operating between 30 and 88 MHz. It elevates the antenna radiating elements up to 30 feet above ground level using sectional aluminum mast poles, greatly extending communication range over flat and rolling terrain. The entire system is man-portable and can be erected or struck by a two-soldier team in approximately 15 minutes.

NAME: M9 Multi-Purpose Bayonet System
DESCRIPTION: This is a multipurpose edged combat weapon and field utility tool designed to attach to the muzzle ring and bayonet lug of M16 rifles and M4 carbines. It features a 7-inch stainless steel blade with a sawback spine, an ergonomic thermoplastic grip, and an insulated sheath. When combined with the scabbard lug, the bayonet forms a heavy-duty wire cutter capable of cutting electrified concertina wire.

NAME: M22 7x50 Binocular
DESCRIPTION: This is a ruggedized handheld optical observation device offering 7x magnification and 50mm objective lenses for target observation and surveillance. It incorporates built-in reticle markings that allow soldiers to estimate range and direct artillery or mortar fire onto enemy positions. The optics are nitrogen-purged, waterproof, and equipped with laser protection filters to guard the user's eyes against battlefield laser threats.

NAME: M1077A1 General Purpose Flatrack
DESCRIPTION: This is a heavy-duty steel and aluminum cargo-carrying platform designed for use with the Palletized Load System (PLS) and HEMTT Load Handling System (LHS). It allows rapid self-loading, transport, and offloading of up to 16.5 tons of ammunition, rations, and bulk supplies without requiring forklift support. The unit features downward-folding side gates and tie-down points to secure diverse cargo configurations.

NAME: AN/PYQ-10 Simple Key Loader (SKL)
DESCRIPTION: This is a ruggedized handheld cryptographic device used to store, manage, and distribute electronic communications security (COMSEC) keys and mission initialization data. It interfaces with tactical radios, GPS receivers, and secure computing platforms to enable encrypted communications and secure networks. The system operates on a hardened operating system and features an integrated stylus touchscreen.

NAME: Mounted Family of Computer Systems (MFoCS)
DESCRIPTION: This is a modular, ruggedized computing architecture engineered for integration into tactical combat and wheeled vehicles. It provides tactical mission command processing, blue-force situational awareness, and navigation displays for vehicle commanders. The system is designed to withstand extreme thermal, shock, and vibrational stresses of off-road tactical operations.

NAME: Tactical Digital Computer System
DESCRIPTION: This is a military-grade computing workstation designed for deployment in tactical command posts and field operations centers. It processes, analyzes, and displays command, control, and battlefield sensor information for staff officers and commanders. The hardware features tamper-resistant enclosures, secure boot features, and shock-mounted components.

NAME: Tactical Digital Computer System
DESCRIPTION: This is a ruggedized digital computing platform used within mission command networks to execute specialized tactical software applications. It provides high-speed data processing, networking connectivity, and secure digital storage in mobile shelter configurations. The system is hardened against extreme environmental conditions and electromagnetic interference.

NAME: OL-605/TYQ Digital Computer System
DESCRIPTION: This is a specialized shelter-mounted computing and data distribution terminal used within tactical command post systems. It integrates diverse sensor feeds, communications links, and operational databases to deliver consolidated common operational picture data. The system utilizes military standard interconnects to interface directly with tactical local area networks.

NAME: Tactical Digital Computer System
DESCRIPTION: This is a hardened electronic computer system utilized in field tactical environments to support automated mission command functions. It enables real-time transmission of digital fire missions, logistical tracking data, and troop movement reports. The platform is engineered to maintain continuous operation under severe vibration, dust, and temperature extremes.

NAME: Tactical Digital Computer System
DESCRIPTION: This is a rugged mobile data processing computer designed for tactical operations centers and vehicular installations. It hosts mission-essential mission command software to allow commanders to visualize the battlefield and coordinate multi-domain fires and maneuvers. It features dual-display support, integrated cryptographic interfaces, and rapid zeroize capabilities.

NAME: Tactical Digital Computer System
DESCRIPTION: This is an expeditionary tactical computer system engineered for secure digital communications and data processing at battalion and brigade echelons. It provides soldiers with the processing power required to manage intelligence feeds, map overlays, and operational reporting. The enclosure is sealed against moisture and dust and operates reliably on fluctuating tactical electrical grids.

NAME: Tactical Digital Computer System
DESCRIPTION: This is a ruggedized processing terminal deployed across tactical command elements to support decentralized battle management. It interfaces directly with tactical combat net radios to send and receive digital message traffic and situation reports. The hardware meets stringent military environmental standards for drop resistance, water resistance, and wide-range operating temperatures.

NAME: Tactical Digital Computer System
DESCRIPTION: This is a field-deployable digital computer system designed to host tactical servers and client applications in tactical operations centers. It facilitates secure data sharing, voice-over-IP management, and messaging across dispersed tactical units. The system incorporates hot-swappable solid-state drives and redundant cooling to ensure mission continuity.

NAME: Electronic Maintenance Kit
DESCRIPTION: This is a comprehensive field repair and maintenance kit containing specialized electronic tools, soldering equipment, and circuit test fixtures. It is used by communication-electronic repairers to perform direct support repairs on radios, sensors, and electronic assemblies. The kit is housed in an impact-resistant transit case designed for rapid deployment.

NAME: M4A1 Carbine
DESCRIPTION: This is a lightweight, gas-operated, magazine-fed combat carbine chambered in 5.56x45mm NATO with a 14.5-inch barrel and collapsible stock. It is the primary individual combat weapon of the U.S. Army, featuring fully automatic and semi-automatic firing modes. It includes an integrated Picatinny rail receiver to mount close-combat optics, thermal sights, laser aiming devices, and grenade launchers, with an effective point-target range of 500 meters.

NAME: Tactical Digital Computer System
DESCRIPTION: This is a ruggedized military computing system designed to support digital mission command and tactical network routing. It interfaces with tactical radios, local area networks, and visual display units to present situational awareness data to mission commanders. The system is hardened against shock, dust, and moisture for reliable operation in combat environments.

NAME: Shop Equipment, Electrical Repair
DESCRIPTION: This is a modular maintenance shop set providing specialized workbenches, testing instruments, power supplies, and hand tools for electrical repairs. It enables military technicians to troubleshoot vehicle wiring harnesses, alternators, starter motors, and electrical distribution panels in field conditions. The shop set is organized into portable storage chests for transport in maintenance vehicles.

NAME: Field Dental Operating Unit
DESCRIPTION: A portable, fully functional dental chair and equipment set used by military dentists in field hospitals. It provides suction, air, and water necessary for performing restorative dentistry and oral surgery in austere environments.

NAME: TS-4084/G Distortion Analyzer
DESCRIPTION: This is a precision electronic test set used to quantify audio harmonic distortion, frequency response, and noise levels in communications equipment. It is employed by communications technicians to calibrate and ensure the voice intelligibility and data accuracy of tactical transceivers and secure telephone links. The device is built into a ruggedized case suitable for field maintenance.

NAME: TS-4348/UV Optical/Electro-Optical Test Set
DESCRIPTION: This is a specialized diagnostic test apparatus used to align, inspect, and evaluate electro-optical sights, thermal imagers, and night vision devices. It generates calibrated light sources and optical targets to measure resolution, focus, and tube performance during scheduled maintenance. It ensures that night vision devices meet operational standards before issue to combat troops.

NAME: KG-175D TACLANE Network Encryptor
DESCRIPTION: This is a high-speed, Type 1 certified inline network encryptor that provides secure data communications over Internet Protocol networks. It encrypts classified traffic up to the Top Secret level across tactical local area networks and wide area satellite links. The device is compact, low power, and designed for installation in mobile shelter server racks or vehicle command systems.

NAME: Fire Extinguisher Refill and Service System
DESCRIPTION: This is a specialized maintenance system designed to recharge, inspect, and pressurize combat vehicle automatic fire extinguishing bottles and handheld extinguishers. It handles standard military extinguishing agents such as Halon replacements and dry chemicals in accordance with strict safety procedures. The equipment ensures tactical combat vehicles maintain operational fire suppression readiness in the field.

NAME: PDISE 40-Amp Electrical Distribution System
DESCRIPTION: This is a portable Power Distribution Illumination System, Electrical (PDISE) package rated for 40-amp branch circuits. It safely distributes electrical power from tactical diesel generators to command tents, lighting strings, and sensitive electronic workstations. The system includes circuit breakers, weatherproof junction boxes, and heavy-duty cabling.

NAME: M7 Forward Repair System (FRS)
DESCRIPTION: This is a heavy-duty, containerized mobile maintenance workshop mounted on an M1077 flatrack deployable by Palletized Load System (PLS) or HEMTT LHS trucks. It features an onboard 35-kW diesel generator, an industrial air compressor, a multi-process welder, and a 5-ton hydraulic crane with a 14-foot reach. It provides maintenance companies with comprehensive on-site battlefield recovery, cutting, and repair capabilities for heavy combat vehicles.

NAME: SG-1264/U Radio Frequency Signal Generator
DESCRIPTION: This is a precision electronic test instrument that produces calibrated continuous wave and modulated radio frequency signals across military communication bands. It is utilized in field and depot maintenance shops to align, calibrate, and troubleshoot radio receivers and signal processing systems. The unit features precise frequency synthesis and attenuation controls within a ruggedized chassis.

NAME: MEP-803A 10-kW Tactical Quiet Generator Set
DESCRIPTION: This is a skid-mounted, fully enclosed diesel-engine-driven generator that produces 10 kilowatts of 60 Hz electrical power at standard military voltages. It is engineered with acoustic dampening materials to provide a low acoustic signature, making it virtually undetectable at tactical distances. It is widely used to power tactical command posts, medical units, and maintenance support facilities.

NAME: MEP-831A 3-kW Tactical Quiet Generator Set
DESCRIPTION: This is a compact, single-cylinder diesel-engine-driven generator set designed to supply 3 kilowatts of 60 Hz electrical power. Featuring a lightweight frame and sound-attenuating enclosure, it can be easily moved by two soldiers or transported on small tactical trailers. It provides reliable prime power for small command posts, forward communication relays, and weapon charging systems.

NAME: MEP-802A 5-kW Tactical Quiet Generator Set
DESCRIPTION: This is a rugged 5-kilowatt, 60 Hz tactical diesel generator set designed for expeditionary operations. It features acoustic suppression that minimizes noise detection on the battlefield and operates on standard military diesel and JP-8 fuels. The generator supplies continuous prime power to small tactical units, surveillance radars, and communication shelters.

NAME: MEP-806A 60-kW Tactical Quiet Generator Set
DESCRIPTION: This is a heavy tactical diesel generator set that delivers 60 kilowatts of 120/208V or 240/416V three-phase electrical power. Designed for continuous heavy-duty service, it powers large command complexes, air defense radars, and heavy maintenance workshops. It is equipped with advanced sound-deadening panels, digital power management controls, and external fuel connection provisions.

NAME: Space Heater Convective (SHC) 120,000 BTU
DESCRIPTION: This is an external, ducted diesel-fueled space heater capable of delivering up to 120,000 BTU/hr of forced warm air. It operates on military diesel or kerosene and connects to field shelters and tents via flexible ducting to keep exhaust fumes outside. The heater includes thermostatic controls and automated safety shut-offs for safe, continuous cold-weather heating.

NAME: Ducted Tent Heater (DTH-350) 350,000 BTU
DESCRIPTION: This is a high-capacity, heavy-duty ducted space heater engineered to provide 350,000 BTU/hr of heated air to large tactical tents and maintenance shelters. It runs on liquid military fuels such as JP-8 and diesel, using high-volume blower fans to circulate heat through multiple distribution ducts. It is essential for sustaining maintenance and command operations in arctic and severe winter conditions.

NAME: AN/ASM-146B Electronics Shop
DESCRIPTION: This is a mobile, shelter-mounted electronics maintenance facility mounted on a tactical vehicle chassis. It is equipped with specialized work stations, precision instruments, and diagnostic equipment used to repair avionic communication, navigation, and surveillance systems. The shelter provides a climate-controlled and electromagnetically shielded environment for sensitive electronic maintenance.

NAME: AN/ASM-147B Electronics Shop
DESCRIPTION: This is a transportable tactical shelter configured as a specialized electronics and avionics maintenance workshop. It contains test benches, power supplies, calibration tools, and replacement components required to perform field maintenance on aircraft electrical and avionics subsystems. The shelter is transportable by tactical cargo trucks or cargo helicopters.

NAME: Shop Equipment, Hydraulic Systems Repair
DESCRIPTION: This is a specialized mobile maintenance shop set containing hydraulic test stands, pressure gauges, hose crimpers, and flushing units. It allows mechanics to diagnose leaks, measure hydraulic pump pressures, and fabricate replacement high-pressure hoses for combat and engineering vehicles. The set is packaged in transportable modular containers for forward deployment.

NAME: M22 Automatic Chemical Agent Detector Alarm (ACADA)
DESCRIPTION: This is an automated, standalone chemical warfare agent point-detection and alarm system. It continuously samples ambient air to detect, identify, and alert personnel to the presence of nerve and blister agent vapors using ion mobility spectrometry. The system can operate on vehicle mounts or tripod ground installations, sounding audible and visual alarms while transmitting warning data across tactical networks.

NAME: M26 Joint Service Transportable Decontamination System Small Scale (JSTDS-SS)
DESCRIPTION: This is a portable, diesel-engine-powered decontamination apparatus designed to decontaminate vehicles, equipment, weapons, and terrain exposed to CBRN agents. It features high-pressure hot water delivery, chemical decontaminant applicators, and water extraction systems mounted in a compact footprint. The system can be carried in the back of a light tactical vehicle or utility trailer for rapid response.

NAME: AN/TSC-185 Satellite Communications Terminal
DESCRIPTION: This is a mobile, heavy-duty tactical satellite communications terminal that provides wideband Beyond-Line-of-Sight (BLOS) connectivity for brigade and division command posts. It operates across multiple frequency bands (X, Ku, and Ka) to connect tactical local area networks to the Department of Defense Information Network. The terminal is transportable by tactical vehicles and can be deployed rapidly in the field.

NAME: Tactical Electrical Load Bank
DESCRIPTION: This is a portable testing device containing resistive and reactive load elements used to test and calibrate tactical diesel generator sets under controlled electrical loads. It ensures generators operate efficiently at full rated capacity and prevents engine "wet stacking" caused by running generators under light loads. The unit includes monitoring instruments to measure voltage, frequency, and current draw.

NAME: M320A1 Grenade Launcher Module
DESCRIPTION: This is a single-shot, 40x46mm low-velocity grenade launcher that can be mounted under the barrel of an M4A1 carbine or configured with a buttstock as a standalone shoulder-fired weapon. It features a side-loading rifled barrel that accommodates longer non-lethal, illumination, and specialized explosive munitions, replacing the older M203. It includes an integrated day/night sighting system with laser rangefinding capability out to an effective range of 400 meters.

NAME: AN/USM-717 Digital Multimeter
DESCRIPTION: This is a ruggedized, handheld electronic measuring instrument used to test AC/DC voltage, current, resistance, capacitance, and continuity in tactical equipment. It is engineered with sealed casing and shock absorption to survive field use by vehicle mechanics and communications repairers. The device provides precise digital readouts and automated diagnostic measurements.

NAME: Shop Equipment, Metal Working
DESCRIPTION: This is a deployable machine shop set that includes metal lathes, milling attachments, drill presses, and metal-cutting saws. It enables machinists and maintenance technicians to fabricate, modify, and repair metal components and vehicle parts directly in forward tactical areas. The set is typically housed in an expandable mobile shelter or containerized facility.

NAME: Shop Equipment, Metal Working Maintenance
DESCRIPTION: This is a specialized metalworking and fabrication shop set providing specialized measuring instruments, cutters, taps, dies, and hand tools for metal fabrication. It complements field repair operations by allowing soldiers to manufacture bespoke brackets, structural repairs, and armor components. The tools are arranged in ruggedized transit cases for rapid movement.

NAME: Tactical Software System
DESCRIPTION: This entry represents an authorized operational software suite or distribution package for tactical computing devices and mission command servers. It provides the operating environment, device drivers, and applications needed to interface tactical hardware with mission networks. Tactical software is strictly controlled for COMSEC compliance and operational cybersecurity.

NAME: Small Arms Optical Boresight (SAB)
DESCRIPTION: This is a portable optical boresighting kit designed to align the iron sights, reflex sights, laser pointers, and thermal optics of small arms without firing live ammunition. It utilizes precision optical mandrels that insert into the weapon's barrel to project a calibrated reticle pattern, saving time and ammunition during zeroing. The kit accommodates multiple weapon calibers including 5.56mm, 7.62mm, and .50 caliber.

NAME: M249 Squad Automatic Weapon (SAW)
DESCRIPTION: This is a gas-operated, air-cooled, magazine- or belt-fed light machine gun chambered in 5.56x45mm NATO. It provides infantry fire teams with a high volume of suppressive fire at cyclic rates of approximately 850 rounds per minute. Operated by a single gunner, it features an integrated folding bipod, rapid-change barrel, and an effective range of 800 meters for point targets and 1,000 meters for area targets.

NAME: MK93 Mod 2 Machine Gun Mount
DESCRIPTION: This is a universal soft-mount weapon cradle engineered to accept either an M2A1 .50 caliber heavy machine gun or an MK19 40mm automatic grenade launcher. It incorporates hydraulic recoil dampening buffers that absorb substantial firing shock, dramatically increasing weapon controllability, tracking, and target accuracy. The mount can be installed on standard vehicle ring mounts, pedestal stands, and tactical ground tripods.

NAME: M50 Joint Service General Purpose Mask (JSGPM)
DESCRIPTION: This is the standard individual protective mask providing face, eye, and respiratory defense against chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN) agents and toxic industrial materials. It features dual conformal M61 filter canisters mounted on the cheeks, providing low breathing resistance, improved weapon cheek weld, and a wide panoramic field of view. The mask includes an integrated drinking tube, voice projection port, and communications interface.

NAME: Measuring Tool Set, Machinist
DESCRIPTION: This is a precision measuring set containing micrometers, vernier calipers, depth gauges, dial indicators, and thread pitch gauges. It is used by military machinists and maintenance technicians to perform ultra-precise dimensional inspections of engine, weapon, and transmission components. The set is protected inside a cushioned wooden or aluminum instrument case.

NAME: M249 Light Machine Gun (Para Variant)
DESCRIPTION: This is a compact configuration of the 5.56x45mm Squad Automatic Weapon featuring a shortened barrel and a collapsible aluminum buttstock. It was engineered for paratroopers, mechanized infantry, and urban combat teams requiring high-volume suppressive fire in confined spaces. It fires standard 5.56mm linked belts or M16/M4 magazines and retains full compatibility with vehicle mounts and weapon optics.

NAME: M2A1 .50 Caliber Heavy Machine Gun
DESCRIPTION: This is an air-cooled, recoil-operated, belt-fed heavy machine gun chambered in .50 BMG (12.7x99mm NATO) with a cyclic rate of 450 to 600 rounds per minute. The modern M2A1 upgrade incorporates a quick-change barrel with fixed headspace and timing, a flash suppressor, and a folding carrying handle to eliminate user headspace errors and enhance crew safety. It delivers devastating direct fire against personnel, light armored vehicles, and low-flying aircraft at ranges exceeding 1,800 meters.

NAME: M192 Lightweight Ground Mount
DESCRIPTION: This is a lightweight tactical ground tripod designed to replace the legacy M122 tripod for mounting M249 and M240B machine guns. Constructed from high-strength aluminum and titanium, it weighs less than 12 pounds while folding into a compact, easily transportable configuration. It features integrated traverse and elevation mechanisms with an intuitive clutch lock that allows rapid tracking and precise sector engagement.

NAME: M66 Ring Mount
DESCRIPTION: This is a 360-degree rotating ring mount assembly installed over the roof hatch of tactical wheeled vehicles, including FMTV and HEMTT trucks. It serves as the mechanical base for weapon cradles to mount M2 .50 caliber machine guns, MK19 grenade launchers, or M240 machine guns for vehicle self-defense. The gunner operates within the ring, which features roller bearings and brake locks for smooth rotation and stable firing.

NAME: AN/PVS-14 Monocular Night Vision Device (MNVD)
DESCRIPTION: This is a lightweight, passive generation-3 image-intensified night vision device used for dismounted night navigation, surveillance, and weapon aiming. It can be handheld, worn on a soldier's helmet mount, or affixed to an individual weapon rail behind an optical sight. Powered by a single AA battery, it incorporates an integrated infrared illuminator and gain control to provide clear vision in near-total darkness.

NAME: MK19 Mod 3 40mm Automatic Grenade Launcher
DESCRIPTION: This is an air-cooled, blowback-operated, disintegrating-link belt-fed automatic weapon that fires 40mm high-velocity grenade munitions at a cyclic rate of 325 to 375 rounds per minute. It is capable of engaging point targets at ranges up to 1,500 meters and area targets up to 2,212 meters with high-explosive dual-purpose (HEDP) rounds that defeat light armor and personnel. The weapon is typically deployed on tripods or mounted on tactical combat vehicles.

NAME: M240B Medium Machine Gun
DESCRIPTION: This is a continuous-fire, gas-operated, belt-fed medium machine gun chambered in 7.62x51mm NATO, serving as the standard squad and platoon suppression weapon. It features a durable steel receiver, hydraulic recoil buffer, front barrel heat shield with integrated accessory rails, and an integral bipod. It fires at a cyclic rate of 650 to 950 rounds per minute, delivering accurate suppressive fire out to 800 meters against point targets and 1,800 meters against area targets on a tripod.

NAME: AN/PSN-13A Defense Advanced GPS Receiver (DAGR)
DESCRIPTION: This is an upgraded configuration of the handheld military Global Positioning System receiver designed for enhanced satellite acquisition and anti-jamming performance. It processes selective availability and anti-spoofing cryptographic signals to deliver exact coordinates and navigation routes across denied environments. The device can store multiple waypoints, interface with vehicular power, and exchange target data with laser designators.

NAME: M17 Modular Handgun System (MHS)
DESCRIPTION: This is a full-size, striker-fired 9x19mm NATO semi-automatic service pistol adopted as the primary sidearm of the U.S. Army to replace the M9. Based on the SIG Sauer P320 platform, it features a polymer grip frame with interchangeable grip modules, an ambidextrous manual safety, night sights, and an optic-ready slide. It is issued with one standard 17-round flush magazine and two extended 21-round magazines.

NAME: AN/USM-708 Digital Oscilloscope Set
DESCRIPTION: This is a rugged, multi-channel portable electronic oscilloscope used by maintenance personnel to capture, display, and analyze complex electrical waveforms. It enables precision diagnosis of digital and analog circuits inside tactical weapon systems, communications networks, and vehicular electronic systems. The unit comes equipped with shielded test probes and is sealed to operate in harsh field repair shops.

NAME: PP-8498/U Tactical Power Supply
DESCRIPTION: This is a regulated military DC power supply that converts standard alternating current (AC) generator or commercial power into stable 28-volt direct current (DC). It is used to bench-test tactical vehicle electronics, communications shelters, and avionics systems without discharging onboard vehicle batteries. The unit features built-in overload and short-circuit protection for equipment safety.

NAME: M28 Purging and Charging Unit
DESCRIPTION: This is a specialized pneumatic service apparatus used by optical maintenance technicians to evacuate moisture from optical fire control instruments and recharge them with dry nitrogen. It prevents internal fogging, corrosion, and optical distortion on laser rangefinders, thermal sights, and tank periscopes exposed to wide temperature changes. The unit includes high-pressure nitrogen regulators, valves, and precision hoses.

NAME: OL-588/TYQ Signal Processor Group
DESCRIPTION: This is a shelter-mounted electronic signal processing subsystem used in tactical intelligence and air defense radar ground stations. It filters, demodulates, and processes incoming raw radar and radio frequency signals into digitized data for operator analysis. The unit is built into standard shock-isolated electronics racks within tactical command shelters.

NAME: Refrigeration and HVAC Maintenance Tool Kit
DESCRIPTION: This is a specialized technician tool kit containing vacuum pumps, manifold gauge sets, recovery cylinders, and flaring tools designed to service tactical environmental control units (ECUs). It allows refrigeration specialists to diagnose refrigerant leaks, evacuate contaminated lines, and recharge military air conditioning systems with EPA-approved refrigerants. The tools are organized in weather-sealed hard cases for field use.

NAME: Optical Time-Domain Reflectometer (OTDR) Set
DESCRIPTION: This is an electro-optical diagnostic instrument used to test the integrity, loss, and continuity of tactical fiber optic communications cables. It injects light pulses into optical fiber lines and measures the reflected return to pinpoint cable breaks, splice losses, and dirty connectors. The device is essential for setting up and troubleshooting tactical local area networks in expeditionary command posts.

NAME: AN/VDR-2 Radiac Set
DESCRIPTION: This is a tactical radiation detection, indication, and computation system that can be mounted in combat vehicles or carried in a dismounted configuration. It measures ambient gamma dose rates and detects low-energy beta radiation contamination on personnel and equipment after a nuclear or radiological event. It features an external detector probe, a digital display box, and adjustable audio-visual alarm thresholds to protect soldier health.

NAME: AN/PDR-77 Radiac Set
DESCRIPTION: This is a portable, modular radiation survey meter designed to identify and measure alpha, beta, gamma, and X-ray radiation using interchangeable detector probes. It is used by CBRN specialists to perform precision radiation surveys on personnel, equipment, food, and water following nuclear fallout or industrial accidents. The system stores historical survey readings and is housed in a ruggedized transit case.

NAME: AN/UDR-13 Pocket Radiac
DESCRIPTION: This is a compact, lightweight radiation detector designed to be carried in a uniform pocket or mounted onto combat equipment. It continuously monitors and displays prompt gamma dose rates as well as total cumulative gamma/neutron radiation doses absorbed over time. It provides frontline troops with immediate situational awareness of radiological hazards through audible alarms and back-lit digital readouts.

NAME: AN/GRM-122 Radio Test Set
DESCRIPTION: This is an automated radio test station specifically designed to troubleshoot, calibrate, and verify the performance of Single Channel Ground and Airborne Radio System (SINCGARS) transceivers and power amplifiers. It automates testing sequences for receiver sensitivity, transmitter power, and frequency-hopping synchronization, reducing repair time for communications maintenance technicians. The unit is housed in a heavy-duty portable aluminum enclosure.

NAME: AN/VRC-89F Vehicular Radio Set
DESCRIPTION: This is a vehicular dual-transceiver SINCGARS VHF-FM tactical radio installation comprising two RT-1523 transceivers, a vehicular amplifier adapter, and a 50-watt power amplifier. It allows a tactical vehicle crew to monitor and transmit on two separate tactical frequency nets simultaneously, such as a company command net and a fire support net. It operates across 30 to 87.975 MHz with integrated frequency hopping and Type 1 encryption.

NAME: AN/VRC-92F Vehicular Radio Set
DESCRIPTION: This is a dual-transceiver, long-range vehicular SINCGARS VHF-FM radio system featuring two RT-1523 transceivers and two 50-watt power amplifiers. It is configured to operate either as two high-power mobile voice/data nodes or as an automated tactical radio retransmission (retrans) station to bridge communications across long distances or obstructed terrain. The installation is commonly mounted in command and communication tactical vehicles.

NAME: AN/VRC-90F Vehicular Radio Set
DESCRIPTION: This is a vehicular single-transceiver long-range SINCGARS VHF-FM tactical radio installation consisting of one RT-1523 receiver-transmitter and an external 50-watt power amplifier. It is installed in tactical wheeled and tracked vehicles to provide extended-range line-of-sight voice and data communications across the 30 to 87.975 MHz band. The system features electronic counter-countermeasures (ECCM) and secure cryptographic capabilities.

NAME: S-788/G Lightweight Multipurpose Shelter (LMS)
DESCRIPTION: This is a rigid-wall, lightweight aluminum tactical equipment shelter designed to mount directly onto the cargo bed of an M1152A1 HMMWV. It provides a weather-tight, climate-controlled, and electromagnetically shielded workspace for tactical command, communications, and electronics maintenance systems. The shelter features internal mounting rails and cable access bulkheads to facilitate mission hardware installations.

NAME: Standard Automotive Tool Set (SATS)
DESCRIPTION: This is the Army's standard mobile automotive maintenance workshop, typically consisting of a specialized trailer carrying modular weather-resistant tool chests. It provides maintenance companies with thousands of specialized pneumatic tools, hand tools, pullers, and diagnostic equipment needed to repair wheeled and tracked combat fleets. It enables comprehensive field-level maintenance operations without needing a permanent motor pool building.

NAME: M150 Rifle Combat Optic (RCO)
DESCRIPTION: This is a fixed 4x magnification optical combat sight manufactured by Trijicon (ACOG) and adopted for standard issue on M4A1 carbines and M16 rifles. It features a dual-illuminated chevron reticle powered by external fiber optics in daylight and radioactive tritium in total darkness, eliminating battery dependencies. The sight incorporates bullet drop compensation marks out to 800 meters and supports rapid two-eyes-open target engagement using the Bindon Aiming Concept.

NAME: M68 Close Combat Optic (CCO)
DESCRIPTION: This is an unmagnified (1x) red-dot reflex optical sight designed to mount onto the Picatinny rail of M4A1 carbines and M16 rifles for rapid close-quarters target acquisition. It projects an illuminated 2-MOA red aiming dot that allows soldiers to engage targets rapidly with both eyes open while maintaining situational awareness. The optic is submersible, shockproof, compatible with night vision devices, and provides thousands of hours of continuous operation from a single battery.

NAME: M172A1 25-Ton Lowbed Semitrailer
DESCRIPTION: This is a heavy-duty, dual-axle lowbed semitrailer designed to transport engineer construction equipment, combat engineer vehicles, and heavy plant equipment weighing up to 25 tons. It features a low-profile loading deck and hinged rear ramps that permit drive-on loading of tracked bulldozers, graders, and rollers. Towed by standard 5-ton tactical truck tractors, it provides critical logistics and mobility support on highway and unimproved road routes.

NAME: M129A4 12-Ton Van Semitrailer
DESCRIPTION: This is an enclosed dual-axle van semitrailer with a 12-ton cargo capacity, designed to be towed by 5-ton tactical truck tractors. It provides a secure, weatherproof enclosure for transporting bulk spare parts, electronics, mobile maintenance shops, or tactical operations center gear. The interior is fitted with side and rear cargo doors, internal tie-down rings, and interior lighting connections.

NAME: AN/PAS-13B(V)2 Medium Weapon Thermal Sight (MWTS)
DESCRIPTION: This is an uncooled forward-looking infrared thermal sight designed for mounting on squad-level automatic weapons including the M249 SAW and M240B machine gun. It allows gunners to detect, recognize, and accurately engage enemy targets through total darkness, fog, dust, and battlefield smoke screens. The optic features selectable reticles, electronic magnification, and operates silently on standard military batteries.

NAME: AN/PAS-13B(V)3 Heavy Weapon Thermal Sight (HWTS)
DESCRIPTION: This is a high-resolution, long-range uncooled thermal imaging sight developed for crew-served heavy weapons such as the M2A1 .50 caliber machine gun and MK19 40mm automatic grenade launcher. It provides wide and narrow fields of view with electronic zoom, enabling gunners to identify combat targets at ranges exceeding 2,000 meters in zero-visibility conditions. The sight mounts directly to weapon receiver rails and displays digital ballistic aiming reticles.

NAME: AN/PRM-36 Radio Test Set
DESCRIPTION: This is a portable radio frequency diagnostic test set used by field communications maintainers to verify the performance of tactical combat net radios. It tests transmitter output power, frequency accuracy, and modulation characteristics on tactical transceivers like the SINCGARS series. The self-contained unit is housed in an impact-resistant transit case designed for austere flightline and motor pool operations.

NAME: AN/USM-670 Electronic Systems Test Set
DESCRIPTION: This is an automated electronic test and diagnostic station used to troubleshoot and verify line-replaceable units (LRUs) on tactical ground combat vehicles. It runs automated software test scripts that pinpoint electronic component failures, reducing vehicle downtime during field maintenance. The system is protected in a ruggedized, weather-tight transit case.

NAME: Electronic Systems Diagnostic Test Set
DESCRIPTION: This is a multi-purpose field test set used by electronic maintenance technicians to test, align, and diagnose vehicle weapon control boxes, sensor units, and power regulators. It features multi-pin interface cables and programmable diagnostic routines to isolate wiring and module faults. The system is engineered to operate in mobile shop vans and tactical maintenance facilities.

NAME: General Mechanic's Tool Kit (GMTK)
DESCRIPTION: This is the Army's standard-issue general mechanic's tool kit, containing a comprehensive selection of SAE and metric hand tools, wrenches, sockets, pliers, and screwdrivers. It is issued to wheeled and tracked vehicle mechanics to perform scheduled services and field-level vehicle repairs. All tools are organized in custom high-density foam cutouts inside a durable, water-resistant wheeled field case.

NAME: Standard Automotive Tool Set (SATS) Specialty Tool Set
DESCRIPTION: This is a specialized supplemental tool kit supporting the Standard Automotive Tool Set, containing heavy pullers, torque multipliers, bearing drivers, and hydraulic press tools. It enables automotive repairers to perform complex engine replacements, axle overhauls, and transmission repairs on tactical vehicle fleets. The components are stored in organized, heavy-duty mobile tool drawers.

NAME: M1152A1 Expanded Capacity Utility HMMWV
DESCRIPTION: This is an up-armored two-man light tactical vehicle featuring an open rear cargo bed designed to carry troop seating, bulk supplies, or specialized mission equipment. It can be outfitted with the S-788 Lightweight Multipurpose Shelter or utilized as a prime mover for light tactical trailers, handling payloads in excess of 5,000 pounds. The vehicle is protected with armor-ready modular cabin components and a reinforced suspension.

NAME: MEP-804A 15-kW Tactical Quiet Generator Set
DESCRIPTION: This is a fully enclosed, skid-mounted diesel generator set that delivers 15 kilowatts of reliable 60 Hz electrical power. It features advanced acoustic dampening panels to reduce detectable sound, allowing it to support forward command posts and sensor stations without compromising tactical positions. The unit operates on military diesel and JP-8 fuels and features comprehensive digital instrumentation.

NAME: MEP-806B 60-kW Tactical Quiet Generator Set
DESCRIPTION: This is a heavy-duty, skid-mounted tactical diesel generator that produces 60 kilowatts of 120/208V or 240/416V three-phase electrical power. Engineered for heavy industrial duty, it powers brigade-level tactical operations centers, air defense radar nodes, and field hospital facilities. The generator includes digital control systems, automatic safety shutdowns, and an acoustic enclosure that minimizes thermal and sound signatures.

NAME: M1083A1 5-Ton Cargo Truck
DESCRIPTION: This is the standard 6x6 cargo truck of the Family of Medium Tactical Vehicles (FMTV), configured without a self-recovery winch. It is designed to transport a 5-ton payload of troops, equipment, and palletized supplies across all types of unimproved roads and cross-country terrain. The vehicle is powered by a Caterpillar turbo-diesel engine with an automatic transmission and includes a Central Tire Inflation System (CTIS).

NAME: M1120A4 HEMTT Load Handling System (LHS)
DESCRIPTION: This is an 8x8 heavy tactical truck equipped with an integrated hydraulic hook-arm load handling system capable of loading, transporting, and offloading flatracks and ISO containers up to 11 tons. It allows a single driver to pick up and drop cargo platforms in seconds without leaving the cab, drastically accelerating logistics turnaround times. The A4 model features an upgraded 500-hp Caterpillar engine, an air-ride suspension, and an armor-ready cab.

NAME: TK-17 Electrical Tool Kit
DESCRIPTION: This is a compact, portable field tool kit equipped with specialized wire strippers, crimpers, heat guns, multimeter leads, and terminal repair parts. It is used by communications-electronics specialists and vehicle mechanics to repair damaged wiring harnesses, splices, and terminal blocks in tactical equipment. The kit is packaged in an impact-resistant field case with compartmentalized storage.

NAME: M1078A1P2 2.5-Ton Cargo Truck (LMTV)
DESCRIPTION: This is a 4x4 Light Medium Tactical Vehicle (LMTV) cargo truck featuring the Long-Term Armor Strategy (LTAS) cab architecture, configured without a winch. It has a payload capacity of 2.5 tons (5,000 lbs) and is used to transport soldiers, equipment, and general military supplies in both highway and tactical off-road environments. The cab is designed to accept modular armor kits (B-kit) to protect the crew against small arms fire and fragmentation.

NAME: Guided Missile System Repairman Tool Kit
DESCRIPTION: This is a specialized military technician tool kit containing precision electronic calibration tools, torque screwdrivers, non-magnetic tweezers, and diagnostic leads. It is used by missile maintenance specialists to perform component-level inspection and repair on anti-tank guided missile launchers and pedestal systems. The tools are organized inside a ruggedized field transport chest.

NAME: M145 Machine Gun Optic (MGO)
DESCRIPTION: This is a ruggedized 3.4x magnification optical combat sight developed by ELCAN for use on M240B medium machine guns and M249 squad automatic weapons. It features a heavy-duty rubberized outer cover that protects the optical prism against harsh recoil and field impacts. The reticle includes ballistic drop compensation out to 1,200 meters and features rotary-controlled LED illumination for engaging targets in low light.

NAME: M984A4 HEMTT Wrecker Truck
DESCRIPTION: This is a heavy 8x8 tactical vehicle recovery truck equipped with a heavy-duty hydraulic crane, an underlift tow assembly, and stabilizing outriggers, configured without a self-recovery winch. It is capable of recovering, lifting, and towing disabled medium and heavy tactical wheeled vehicles across rough tactical terrain. The A4 variant includes a 500-horsepower Caterpillar engine, heavy-duty suspension, and an armor-ready cab.

NAME: M1087A1 5-Ton Expandable Van Truck
DESCRIPTION: This is a 6x6 Family of Medium Tactical Vehicles (FMTV) specialty platform featuring mechanically expandable van sides, configured without a self-recovery winch. Once deployed, the sides slide outward to provide a large, climate-controlled, and electromagnetically shielded workspace for mobile tactical operations centers or maintenance shops. The vehicle includes an onboard power distribution box and integrates with standard military tactical air conditioners.

NAME: M4K Light Capability Rough Terrain Forklift (LCRTF)
DESCRIPTION: This is a compact, highly mobile 4x4 rough-terrain forklift featuring an Air-Operational-Apparatus (AOA) package for rapid air mobility and air-drop certification. It provides up to 4,000 pounds of lift capacity, allowing units to load and unload ammunition, pallets, and supplies over muddy, sandy, or steep terrain where commercial forklifts cannot operate. The mast can be tilted and collapsed to facilitate drive-on transport inside C-130 aircraft.

NAME: TS-4317/GRM-114B Radio Test Set
DESCRIPTION: This is a specialized, handheld electronic diagnostic test instrument designed to evaluate and verify the operational readiness of VHF-FM tactical transceivers. It measures transmitter RF power output, reflected power (VSWR), and receiver sensitivity directly at the vehicle or field installation. It enables quick go/no-go troubleshooting of radio installations prior to launching tactical operations.

NAME: M1088A1 5-Ton Truck Tractor
DESCRIPTION: This is a 6x6 tactical truck tractor of the Family of Medium Tactical Vehicles (FMTV), configured without a self-recovery winch. It is equipped with a fifth wheel coupling assembly designed to haul tactical semitrailers such as the M129 van and M172 lowbed over all types of road surfaces. The vehicle is powered by a Caterpillar turbocharged diesel engine and features an automated transmission for ease of operation.

NAME: M1085A1 5-Ton Long Wheelbase Cargo Truck
DESCRIPTION: This is an extended-wheelbase 6x6 tactical cargo truck of the FMTV series with a 20-foot cargo bed, configured without a winch. It is designed to transport bulky cargo, tactical shelters, or up to 20 combat-equipped soldiers over off-road and highway networks. The vehicle shares common driveline, cab, and automotive components with the standard FMTV family for simplified maintenance and logistics.

NAME: M1076 Palletized Load System (PLS) Trailer
DESCRIPTION: This is a three-axle tactical trailer engineered to carry 8x20 foot flatracks or standard ISO cargo containers with a payload capacity of 16.5 tons. It is towed behind M1074 or M1075 Palletized Load System (PLS) trucks, effectively doubling the cargo haul capacity of a single operator. The trailer features a self-steering rear axle and air suspension to maintain stability and maneuverability over rough cross-country terrain.

NAME: M1095 5-Ton MTV Cargo Trailer
DESCRIPTION: This is a dual-axle tactical cargo flatbed trailer designed to be towed by 5-ton Family of Medium Tactical Vehicles (FMTV) cargo trucks. It provides an additional 5-ton (10,000 lb) payload capacity, allowing units to transport ammunition, rations, and field equipment without tying up additional motorized vehicles. It features an air brake system and suspension matched to FMTV truck specifications.

NAME: Test Adapter Set
DESCRIPTION: This is a specialized diagnostic hardware set containing break-out boxes, multi-pin harness adapters, and interface cables. It connects standard military electronic test sets to specific electronic line-replaceable units on combat vehicles and weapon systems. The set enables technicians to monitor internal system voltages and data signals without dismantling assemblies.

NAME: Carpenter's Tool Kit
DESCRIPTION: This is an expeditionary carpentry and woodworking tool set packaged in a durable, compartmentalized transport chest. It includes handsaws, framing hammers, chisels, spirit levels, speed squares, hand planes, and manual drill sets used by combat engineers. The kit provides the tools required to build wooden fortifications, base camp structures, concrete forms, and tactical obstacles.

NAME: TK-100/G Electronic Equipment Tool Kit
DESCRIPTION: This is a standardized military electronics repair tool set equipped with precision insulated screwdrivers, miniature pliers, wire cutters, and soldering irons. It is issued to communications-electronics maintenance technicians to perform bench and field repairs on delicate circuit boards and components. The set is organized inside a heavy-duty portable case with fitted tool pallets.

NAME: TK-105A/G Electronic Equipment Tool Kit
DESCRIPTION: This is a specialized field maintenance tool set tailored for radio and avionics technicians to service tactical communications and navigation hardware. It includes precision alignment tools, coaxial crimpers, wire strippers, and socket drivers required for connector assembly and component repair. The kit is packaged in a shock-resistant field chest with dedicated tool holders.

NAME: General Pipefitter Tool Kit
DESCRIPTION: This is an expeditionary plumbing and piping tool set containing heavy-duty pipe wrenches, pipe cutters, threaders, reamers, and flaring tools. It is used by combat engineer utilities specialists to install, maintain, and repair water distribution systems, fuel piping, and waste plumbing at expeditionary base camps. The tools are organized within a heavy-duty, weather-resistant mobile field chest.

NAME: Small Arms Maintenance Tool Kit
DESCRIPTION: This is an armorer's maintenance tool set containing dedicated punches, specialized armorers' wrenches, cleaning brushes, and alignment fixtures. It is used to perform direct-support and organizational inspection, disassembly, and parts replacement on Army small arms including pistols, rifles, and machine guns. The kit ensures that weapons remain properly gauged, functional, and safe for combat operations.

NAME: Universal Motor Vehicle Towbar
DESCRIPTION: This is a heavy-duty, adjustable steel towbar assembly equipped with interchangeable towing eyes, clevis adapters, and locking pins. It connects tactical wheeled vehicles to a recovery or towing vehicle to safely transport disabled vehicles without requiring a dedicated wrecker. The towbar is collapsible for easy vehicle storage and is rated to handle medium and heavy tactical trucks.

NAME: M149A2 400-Gallon Water Trailer
DESCRIPTION: This is a single-axle tactical trailer featuring an insulated 400-gallon stainless steel tank designed to transport potable drinking water to field units. Colloquially known as the "Water Buffalo," it is equipped with multiple dispensing faucets, an internal heating element to prevent winter freezing, and a rear bumper step for soldier access. It can be towed by standard light and medium tactical vehicles across highway and cross-country terrain.

NAME: M205 Lightweight Tripod Mount
DESCRIPTION: This is a lightweight ground tripod designed to mount heavy weapons, including the M2A1 .50 caliber machine gun and MK19 40mm automatic grenade launcher. Weighing approximately 34 pounds, it is significantly lighter than the legacy M3 tripod, featuring integrated traverse and elevation mechanisms for enhanced gunner accuracy. Its folding leg design allows rapid emplacement and displacement during tactical infantry operations.

NAME: MK-2551/U Accessory Kit, Electrical Equipment
DESCRIPTION: This is a specialized supplemental equipment kit containing auxiliary cables, connectors, adapters, and mounting hardware for tactical electrical assemblies. It is used to connect, interface, and maintain field electrical and communications gear during tactical deployments. The components are housed in a ruggedized transport case to prevent environmental damage.

NAME: AN/USM-686 Spectrum Analyzer Set
DESCRIPTION: This is a precision electronic test instrument designed to measure and display signal amplitude across a wide range of radio frequencies. It is utilized by maintenance personnel to analyze RF transmissions, detect electromagnetic interference, and calibrate tactical communications systems. The ruggedized transit case allows deployment directly into field maintenance environments.

NAME: AN/USM-459 Countermeasures Test Set
DESCRIPTION: This is an intermediate-level electronic test station used to diagnose, verify, and align aviation radar warning and electronic warfare countermeasures equipment. It provides simulated radar and infrared threat signals to confirm that aircraft survivability equipment responds correctly prior to combat missions. The test set is transportable and deployed with aviation maintenance units.

NAME: PDISE 200-Amp 3-Phase Electrical Feeder System
DESCRIPTION: This is a high-capacity electrical distribution feeder system capable of routing 200-amp, three-phase electrical power across tactical base camps and command complexes. It serves as the primary backbone connection between large generator sets and intermediate distribution boxes. The components are weather-sealed, color-coded for safety, and ruggedized to withstand vehicle traffic.

NAME: MEP-805A 30-kW Tactical Quiet Generator Set
DESCRIPTION: This is a medium-capacity diesel-driven generator set providing 30 kilowatts of three-phase electrical power for tactical installations. It features digital engine monitoring, automatic fault protection, and a sound-attenuated housing for low acoustic and thermal signatures. The unit serves as prime power for brigade-level command posts, field hospitals, and large maintenance facilities.

NAME: SG-1171/U Signal Generator
DESCRIPTION: This is an electronic test instrument designed to synthesize stable, high-accuracy radio frequency signals for diagnostic purposes. Communications maintenance specialists use it to verify receiver sensitivity, calibrate frequency synthesizers, and troubleshoot tactical communication lines. It is constructed in an impact-resistant enclosure suited for mobile electronic shop vans.

NAME: AN/PDR-75 Battlefield Dosimeter
DESCRIPTION: This is a tactical radiation dosimeter system designed to measure and record cumulative total doses of neutron and gamma radiation absorbed by individual soldiers. The system includes personal optical dosimeters and an automated reader unit used to monitor radiation exposure levels during nuclear operations. It assists commanders in making risk assessments and triage decisions in radiological environments.

NAME: KIR-1A/TSEC Cryptographic Interrogator
DESCRIPTION: This is a specialized cryptographic computer component integrated into Mark XII Identification Friend or Foe (IFF) interrogator systems. It generates and decodes secure Mode 4 encrypted challenge and reply signals to positively identify friendly aircraft and ground platforms. The unit is critical for preventing fratricide in complex, multi-service combat airspaces.

NAME: All Terrain Lifter Army System (ATLAS II) Forklift
DESCRIPTION: This is a heavy-duty, rough-terrain variable-reach forklift truck capable of lifting up to 10,000 pounds of cargo and materials. It features four-wheel drive, multiple steering modes, and an extendable telescoping boom designed to load and unload cargo from ISO containers, flatracks, and tactical vehicles over rough terrain. It is operated by a single driver inside an armored or ROPS-certified cab.

NAME: Specialized Vehicular Mechanic Tool Kit
DESCRIPTION: This is an advanced set of specialized hand tools, pullers, torque wrenches, and impact sockets designed for direct-support vehicular mechanics. It contains items required to overhaul drive trains, suspension systems, and heavy power packs on wheeled and tracked combat vehicles. The tools are organized into heavy-duty, weather-resistant mobile tool chests.

NAME: Maintenance Kit, Electronic Equipment
DESCRIPTION: This is a portable field maintenance kit containing precision screwdrivers, desoldering pumps, wiring harness tools, and connector repair parts. It is used by avionic and radio technicians to repair damaged wiring and electronic modules on tactical systems. The components are housed in an impact-resistant carrying case with organized storage trays.

NAME: Small Arms Repairman Tool Kit (SARTK)
DESCRIPTION: This is a comprehensive, specialized armorer's tool kit used by military small arms repairers (MOS 91F) to inspect, disassemble, repair, and gage Army weapons. It includes precision headspace and timing gages, armorer wrenches, barrel alignment rods, drift punches, and custom bench fixtures. The kit enables field-level maintenance on rifles, pistols, shotguns, machine guns, and grenade launchers.

NAME: Command Post Computing Environment (CPCE) System
DESCRIPTION: This is an enterprise mission command computing software and hardware suite deployed at battalion, brigade, and division headquarters. It consolidates diverse warfighting tactical systems—including intelligence, fires, maneuvers, and logistics—into a single web-enabled common operational picture. It significantly streamlines command post hardware footprints while improving real-time tactical decision-making.

NAME: Shop Equipment, Contact Maintenance (SECM)
DESCRIPTION: This is a specialized mobile maintenance module mounted on the chassis of an M1152A1 HMMWV to provide rapid forward vehicular repair.
